decision_description: The concept_refiner agent has completed alignment assessment of the MAESTRO concept corpus against all Tier 2B expected outcomes (EO-01, EO-02), scope requirements (SR-01 through SR-12), and call constraints (CC-01 through CC-14). All two expected outcomes are confirmed covered. Of 18 scope and constraint elements assessed: 13 are fully covered, 2 are partially covered (SR-11/CC-11 — in-vehicle autonomous driving sector not addressed as a demonstrator due to absence of automotive consortium partners; WP8 architectural mapping provides partial coverage), and 3 are not applicable (CC-12 FSTP optional mechanism, CC-13 administrative deadline, CC-14 duration confirmed at 48 months). One scope conflict (SCL-01) was identified and resolved: MAESTRO's deliberate omission of an in-vehicle autonomous driving demonstrator is grounded in the portfolio-level nature of SR-11/CC-11, which requires at least one funded proposal per sector across the portfolio rather than requiring every individual proposal to cover all three sectors. The concept explicitly names the gap, explains the rationale (no automotive partners), and references the portfolio coverage mechanism. Strategic differentiation is confirmed through the integrated three-pillar architecture (neuro-symbolic planning, adaptive memory, decentralised multi-agent coordination) unified by a cross-cutting External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, validated across healthcare and advanced manufacturing demonstrators plus a logistics transfer demonstrator.
alternatives_considered: Alternative 1: Treat SR-11/CC-11 partial coverage (no in-vehicle autonomous driving demonstrator) as an unresolved mandatory gap requiring escalation. Rejected because SR-11/CC-11 is explicitly a portfolio-level procedural constraint (procedure_exceptions field in HORIZON-CL4-2026-05-DIGITAL-EMERGING-02.json), not a per-proposal hard mandatory requirement; the concept explicitly acknowledges the gap and provides WP8 architectural mapping as partial coverage with documented rationale.

Alternative 2: Flag CC-12 (FSTP) as a coverage gap requiring the concept to incorporate financial support to third parties. Rejected because CC-12 constraint_type is 'other' and the provision describes maximum amounts available, not a mandatory requirement that all proposals must utilise FSTP; absence of FSTP is a valid design choice.

Alternative 3: Flag the logistics and supply chain transfer demonstrator as out-of-scope because it is not one of the three call-identified portfolio-priority sectors under SR-11. Retained as a flagged borderline item in the scope check (topic-scope-check_a7f1437e.json) but not treated as a hard exclusion, because the activity is a natural extension of SR-02 and SR-07 multi-agent coordination research and the concept frames it explicitly as a transfer demonstrator beyond the minimum sector requirement rather than a primary sector claim.

Alternative 4: Treat the European strategic competitiveness framing (reducing dependency on non-European AI platforms) as an out-of-scope claim. Retained as flagged borderline in the scope check but not escalated as a hard violation, because it is consistent with the general orientation of SR-01 and SR-12 even though no specific Tier 2B scope element positively confirms this framing as an in-scope project objective.

rationale: All two Tier 2B expected outcomes (EO-01, EO-02) are confirmed covered by direct evidence in the MAESTRO concept corpus: EO-01 is addressed by Pillar 1 (neuro-symbolic planning), Pillar 2 (adaptive memory), and the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer; EO-02 is addressed by Pillar 3 (decentralised multi-agent coordination) and the multi-agent extensions of the orchestration layer. All four mandatory scope requirements (SR-01, SR-02, SR-03, SR-04) are fully covered with direct evidence. SR-09 (KPIs and benchmarking) and SR-10 (ADRA/GenAI4EU cohesion tasks) are fully covered. SR-11 (portfolio sector coverage) is partially covered — healthcare and advanced manufacturing demonstrators are confirmed; in-vehicle autonomous driving is not addressed as a demonstrator but is acknowledged explicitly with WP8 architectural mapping as partial coverage. The partial coverage of SR-11/CC-11 is resolved as a deliberate strategic decision grounded in the portfolio-level nature of the constraint: the call's procedure_exceptions field specifies that portfolio coverage is achieved across funded proposals, not required within each individual proposal. The concept's explicit acknowledgement of the gap, documented rationale (no automotive partners), and WP8 partial coverage satisfy the conditions for a resolved strategic decision. All eligibility constraints (CC-09 budget ceiling EUR 19M, CC-10 geographic eligibility, CC-14 duration 48 months) are confirmed met. The concept alignment assessment is complete and the concept is confirmed as aligned with Tier 2B requirements subject to the documented partial coverage of SR-11/CC-11.
